featured_reviews.review_text: The crowd outside this place suggested that the food would be good. I got mutton chops and chicken puffs on New Years Day hoping to enjoy New Years Breakfast with family. Unfortunately 20th Century Super Market was a mistake and left me thoroughly upset with what I got. The mutton chops barely had any stuffing and were coated with soggy bready dough instead of potato. The chicken puffs had some tasteless gelatin like stuffing which left us with a very bad feeling in the mouth. I paid Rs480 for 8 mutton chops and 10 chicken puffs and unfortunately had to trash the food as it was just not edible.

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Sanjeeb Mukherjee
featured_reviews.review_text: Excellent grocery super market and good behavior of all staff.  You will get a discount on each grocery staff compared to any other store. They follow the appropriate COVID guidelines. In addition they provide quick home delivery. Thank you for the great services.

featured_reviews.name: Punit Sahani
featured_reviews.review_text: It's located at Jankalyan Nagar Malad (w). The store is one stop shop for all house hold items and eatables. I would say a D-mart for Jankalyan Nagar, though prices are not as cheap as D-mart. It's a good place to shop and there are on going offers round the year. The quality of products are very good and lot of international variety as well when it comes to chocolates, taste enhancers and ad-ons. The staff is very polite and helpful. Home delivery is available on bill above Rs. 200/- a variety of self grooming products for men and women. I wasn't sure about the store running this long, as plenty other stores had opened before this and all closed down within a short period of time. Their hard work has definitely paid off and the place is always crowded with customers. The store has completely revamped and is better with pay counters and arrangement of products.

featured_reviews.name: Sudhir Raja
featured_reviews.review_text: It's a neat little mini mart that stocks almost everything, as far as one's monthly and daily grocery purchases go. One can also pick up cosmetics, household items such as cleaning tools & liquids, and other essential stuff. All in all, bigger than a corner kirana shop and a condensed version of any large grocery & essentials establishment found at malls. A little congested if packed to the brim, owing to the narrow aisle space but it does the job nevertheless, when you don't want to travel too far. Parking, however, might be an issue for four wheelers, because of the location. They do provide home delivery services within a certain radius, though, so that might be an option to consider. Thanks and stay safe. :)

featured_reviews.name: Komal Shastri
featured_reviews.review_text:
over the years, I have been here so many times and despite the crowd, i still keep coming back. it is genuinely convenient for groceries and even random small things from the stationery or decor section. the store has a little bit of everything, and most of it is basic but useful. from the clothing section, I have bought jeans for my brothers that turned out to be affordable and surprisingly good quality. even the casual tees for both men and women are decent for everyday wear.

I feel, every section has something simple and practical that works well without being overpriced. sometimes you really do not need fancy products for daily use, and D Mart does that part well. definitely not a joke when people say that it is one of those places where you end up buying more than what you came for.

just a suggestion to the management to clear the grocery aisles on the ground floor more regularly. a lot of abandoned carts are left around by random people and they end up blocking the way for days, especially during crowded hours.

featured_reviews.name: Karan Beri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited the Dmart branch in Malad West on a Sunday and honestly it turned out to be one of the most disappointing shopping experiences I have had. I understand weekends are usually crowded, especially Sundays, but proper crowd management and customer service are expected from a well known retail chain like Dmart. Unfortunately this branch failed badly in both areas.
The store was extremely overcrowded to the point where moving from one section to another became stressful and uncomfortable. Long queues were visible everywhere and there seemed to be no proper system to manage the rush. What disappointed me more was the behavior and attitude of some staff members. Many of them looked confused, unorganized and completely unaware of how to handle customers during peak hours. Instead of assisting people properly they appeared irritated and unprofessional.
The worst part of the entire visit was the billing process. It literally took almost one hour just to complete the billing despite standing continuously in the queue. For a retail store of this scale this level of delay is simply unacceptable. There were very few counters operating compared to the crowd present in the store which made the waiting time even more frustrating.
I have personally visited more than 10 Dmart branches across different cities in India and most of them were well managed even during busy hours. That is why this particular experience felt even more shocking and frustrating. Shopping here became more hectic than convenient which should never happen in a supermarket visit.
I hope the management seriously works on improving staff training, customer handling, billing efficiency and crowd management at this branch because the current experience does not match the reputation Dmart usually has across India.

featured_reviews.name: Daksh Kalra
featured_reviews.review_text:
For the longest time, I was a big fan of the Nature’s Basket store at Inorbit Mall, so I was genuinely excited to visit the newly revamped outlet. Unfortunately, the experience was a bit disappointing.

The current product assortment feels quite limited. Their deli meat selection is nowhere close to what you’ll find at Food Square or FreshPik, and I was surprised not to see even basic options like turkey slices.
There were also no fresh dips available during my visit.

Another concern was product freshness. For example, the Healthy Alternatives soya sticks I picked up had been manufactured in February and were due to expire within the next 45 days. I checked for a fresher batch, but none was available.

The fresh cheese section also lacked customer assistance. There was no one available to guide us or offer tastings. Only after I raised the issue with an employee in a very stern way was the manager called over, who then helped us sample a few cheeses (which also wasn’t a super fresh batch,the Gouda with wild herbs)

Overall, the store has great potential, but it would benefit from stronger inventory management, fresher stock rotation, a wider premium food selection, and better-trained staff who can confidently assist customers and enhance the shopping experience.
